summary: OpenAI previewed 'Ultrafast', a new API service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14x faster (750 output tokens/sec) using Cerebras hardware, in limited preview to select customers.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI is deploying Cerebras's wafer-scale accelerator silicon rather than merchant GPU serving to power a new high-speed inference tier for its flagship model.
mechanisms.quote: Powered by Cerebras, Ultrafast generates up to 750 output tokens per second, bringing our most intelligent model to products and workflows where every second matters.

categories.reason: The announcement is a direct demand signal for Cerebras's custom accelerator hardware, deployed to serve OpenAI's frontier model at high speed.
categories.quote: Ultrafast marks the next step in our partnership with Cerebras to bring ultra-low-latency inference to OpenAI’s platform.

practices.reason: Engineers building latency-sensitive products (support, commerce, incident response) now have a concrete option offering up to 14x faster generation at the same model intelligence.
practices.quote: we’re sharing an early look at Ultrafast, a new service tier that runs GPT‑5.6 Sol up to 14× faster than Standard processing

practices.reason: The speed gain is tied to Cerebras's proprietary hardware stack rather than a technique an external team could apply to its own serving infrastructure.
practices.quote: Powered by Cerebras, Ultrafast generates up to 750 output tokens per second

practices.reason: A new API tier is being introduced but remains a limited preview with no general availability yet, so there is no integration work to schedule today.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.6 Sol on Ultrafast mode is available in a limited preview today to a select group of customers.

notable_reason: A frontier lab publicly detailing a production partnership with Cerebras to serve its flagship model is a concrete signal of diversification away from merchant GPU-based inference.
